# Global variables script functions

Functions for C# (`Cb.Call`) and Python (a `cb` method each, or `cb.call`). See [Script functions](index.md) for how to use them.

![A Run Python code step in the action editor](../../assets/screens/actions-python-step.png)

## globals.clearTemporary

Deletes every temporary global variable (the ones that are not saved). Saved ones stay.

**Gives back:** How many variables were deleted.

=== "C#"

    ```csharp
    var answer = await Cb.Call("globals.clearTemporary");
    ```

=== "Python"

    ```python
    answer = cb.globals_clear_temporary()
    ```

## globals.delete

Deletes a global variable.

| Value | In Python | What to put in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `name` | The variable name, like "deaths". |

**Gives back:** true when the variable existed, false when there was nothing to delete.

=== "C#"

    ```csharp
    var answer = await Cb.Call("globals.delete", new { name = "deaths" });
    ```

=== "Python"

    ```python
    answer = cb.globals_delete(name="deaths")
    ```

## globals.get

Reads a global variable as text, the same way ~name~ shows it in a message.

| Value | In Python | What to put in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `name` | The variable name, like "deaths". |

**Gives back:** The value as text, or null when there is no such variable.

=== "C#"

    ```csharp
    var answer = await Cb.Call("globals.get", new { name = "deaths" });
    ```

=== "Python"

    ```python
    answer = cb.globals_get(name="deaths")
    ```

## globals.getValue

Reads a global variable and keeps its type, so a number stays a number and true/false stays true/false.

| Value | In Python | What to put in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `name` | The variable name, like "deaths". |

**Gives back:** The value as a number, true/false or text, or null when there is no such variable.

=== "C#"

    ```csharp
    var answer = await Cb.Call("globals.getValue", new { name = "deaths" });
    ```

=== "Python"

    ```python
    answer = cb.globals_get_value(name="deaths")
    ```

## globals.increment

Adds to a number in a global variable, like a death counter. A missing variable starts at 0. Fails when the variable holds text that is not a number.

| Value | In Python | What to put in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `name` | The variable name, like "deaths". |
| `amount` | `amount` | Optional. How much to add, like 1 or 0.5. Use a negative number to subtract. Leave it out to add 1. |
| `persisted` | `persisted` | Optional. true (the default) saves it so it is still there after a restart; false keeps it only until Cuebot closes. |

**Gives back:** The new value.

=== "C#"

    ```csharp
    var answer = await Cb.Call("globals.increment", new { name = "deaths", amount = 1 });
    ```

=== "Python"

    ```python
    answer = cb.globals_increment(name="deaths", amount=1)
    ```

## globals.set

Saves a value in a global variable. Every action can read it, and messages can show it with ~name~. The value is stored as text.

| Value | In Python | What to put in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `name` | The variable name, like "lastRaider". |
| `value` | `value` | The value to store, like "CoolStreamer". Numbers and true/false are stored as text. |
| `persisted` | `persisted` | Optional. true (the default) saves it so it is still there after a restart; false keeps it only until Cuebot closes. |

**Gives back:** Nothing.

=== "C#"

    ```csharp
    var answer = await Cb.Call("globals.set", new { name = "lastRaider", value = "CoolStreamer" });
    ```

=== "Python"

    ```python
    answer = cb.globals_set(name="lastRaider", value="CoolStreamer")
    ```
